After playing Battlefield 6, I genuinely think Battlefield 2042's maps are well-designed—they're vast and highly playable. They're especially friendly for snipers, with realistic bullet trajectories.
In contrast, in BF6, sniper rifles barely reach 200 meters, and who knows when you'll ever unlock an 8x scope.

After playing Battlefield 2042, I can say the game delivers some really intense and cinematic multiplayer moments. The large-scale battles, explosions, vehicles, and weather effects make matches feel chaotic and exciting, especially when everything is happening at once. The graphics and sound design are impressive, and the modern setting gives access to fun weapons, gadgets, and vehicles. Some maps can feel too large at times, and the game had a rough launch with bugs and performance problems, which many players still remember. However, after updates, the experience feels much better and more enjoyable than before. Overall, Battlefield 2042 may not be the strongest Battlefield game for longtime fans, but it still offers fast-paced action and fun multiplayer moments for players who enjoy large-scale warfare games.

This game actually DEMANDS that you enable Secure Boot in your BIOS to be able to play it...

What... In the actual... Fu(k?!?

Long story short, you are forced to enable Secure Boot in your BIOS, otherwise the game just won't start, and I don't even want to begin listing what's wrong with all of this...

From potentially bricking your Windows install, to a bug found especially in MSI/GIGABYTE motherboards in which after enabling Secure Boot, everything is functional BUT the motherboard doesn't recognize any dedicated GPUs while sometimes not even POSTing (Power-On Self-Test)...

Just...no. I'm gonna stop right here before I get too technical. I mean the list of things that can go wrong by fiddling with the BIOS Secure Boot is so extensive that it's crazy.

Unplayable/10 - Such restrictions can only be implemented by mentally challenged people, so I guess now we finally know what kind of r3tards work at DICE (and EA).

EA changed a lot of things in this game, most notably introducing specialists. I don't like the system much, it's unnecessary for what battlefield was always about, but since they reintroduced main classes recently, they aren't that game impacting anymore. They offer certain subperks/weapons for the classes, but things like the repair tool are standard loadout for every engineer specialist again (as it should always have been). Are specialists ugly visually? definitely, having the same dude in a different outfit running around is an awful concept but imo it impacts the game far less than people think it does.

oh, and don't buy the game for the portal mode. that is probably by far the most justified thing to be upset over with the game, since it's a complete let down and not used much. Suffers from the same thing as every game with a play-into-matchmake button does: Nobody actually uses a server browser anymore, because hitting play is easier.
